directAnswer: Blessed Urban II was Odo of Châtillon, a French monk of Cluny who reigned as pope from 1088 to 1099. He restored the reform papacy after the struggles of Gregory VII's last years and launched the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont in 1095, dying two weeks after crusaders captured Jerusalem.

sections.h2: From Reims and Cluny to Ostia
paras: Odo was born around 1035 in Champagne, near Châtillon-sur-Marne, to a knightly family. He studied at Reims, where St. Bruno, later founder of the Carthusians, was among the teachers, and he served as archdeacon there. He then entered the abbey of Cluny and became its prior under Abbot Hugh.
Gregory VII called him to Rome around 1080 and made him cardinal bishop of Ostia. He served as legate in Germany, where he worked to rally supporters of reform against Henry IV.

Rome was held by the antipope Clement III when Odo was elected at Terracina on March 12, 1088. For years Urban could live in Rome only intermittently. He combined firmness on the principles of reform with a flexible diplomacy, winning back bishops and princes who had wavered and gradually isolating the antipope.

His pontificate also saw the Roman Curia take a more organized form, and the term curia itself becomes common in papal documents in this period. Urban held numerous synods in Italy and France, and he excommunicated King Philip I of France over his marriage to Bertrade of Montfort.

sections.h2: Piacenza, Clermont and the First Crusade
paras: At the Council of Piacenza in March 1095, envoys of the Byzantine emperor Alexios I asked for Western help against the Seljuk Turks. In November 1095 Urban held a council at Clermont in France, and on November 27 he preached in an open field, calling knights to go to the aid of Eastern Christians and to free Jerusalem. Those who went for devotion rather than for glory or gain were promised that the journey would count in place of all penance.

No text of the sermon survives from that day; several chroniclers wrote versions years later, and they differ, though most report the crowd's cry of Deus vult, God wills it. Urban then toured France for months encouraging recruitment.

In 1098 Urban held a council at Bari to discuss differences with the Greek Church, where St. Anselm of Canterbury defended the Western teaching on the procession of the Holy Spirit. The crusaders took Antioch in 1098 and Jerusalem on July 15, 1099, with great bloodshed.

Urban died in Rome on July 29, 1099, before news of Jerusalem's capture could reach him. He was beatified by Pope Leo XIII in 1881, and his feast is kept on July 29. The crusading movement he began remains one of the most debated legacies in Church history.

keyFacts: Born Odo of Châtillon (Lagery) in Champagne, around 1035
Prior of Cluny; made cardinal bishop of Ostia by Gregory VII
Called the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont, November 1095
Held the Council of Bari (1098) with St. Anselm on the filioque

faqs.question: What did Urban II say at Clermont?
faqs.answer: He called on Western knights to aid Eastern Christians and liberate Jerusalem, offering remission of penance to those who went from devotion. The exact wording is unknown, since the surviving accounts were written later and differ from one another.

faqs.question: Did Urban II know that Jerusalem was captured?
faqs.answer: No. Crusaders took Jerusalem on July 15, 1099, and Urban died on July 29, before the news reached Rome.

faqs.question: Why was Urban II elected outside Rome?
faqs.answer: The antipope Clement III, supported by Henry IV, controlled Rome in 1088, so the cardinals met at Terracina to elect him.
